title: Canon layers (Allen-Zhu 2025): a causal depthwise 4-tap convolution on the residual stream before the attention and MLP of every Peri-LN block, on the 107-claude Lean incumbent (4.81M params)
description: New mechanism, no idea ID in the backlog (closest: P29/P38 family). Each of the 6 blocks gets two Canon layers, x_t <- x_t + sum_{i<4} w_i * x_{t-i} (per-channel weights, random init, 12,288 extra params, no extra matmul), before its attention and before its MLP, persisting into RL. Cheap local token mixing gives every position a summary of its 3 predecessors, so attention heads can spend their capacity on long-range citation lookup instead of reconstructing local Lean syntax, which is what Allen-Zhu (2025) reports as raised reasoning depth for small models on synthetic tasks; a deeper effective reasoning depth should give expert iteration more length-7+ proofs to bootstrap from.
hypothesis: In Lean have-chains every line is a short fixed template (have nK : P := rule nI nJ), so much of what each block's attention does is local (what name was just declared, which connective this token sits in, which argument slot is being filled). A 4-tap causal conv on the residual stream does that for free in every block, twice, and the paper's mechanism is that this raises the model's effective reasoning depth (multi-hop composition) at fixed layer count, the axis that helped here (5 -> 6 blocks kept, +16) but costs steps when bought with layers (7 blocks lost 14% of steps). Canon costs almost no steps. Expected signature if right: fewer round-1 parse failures / unbound names than 107 and a higher round-1 targets-solved, carried through the four rounds. If wrong: the random-init conv perturbs the residual stream at the start of a 3,200-step run and the fit is no better, giving a noise-level or negative delta.
expected_delta: +10 mean dev>=7 solves vs 107-claude's 587.00 (range -40 to +45); pretraining steps 3,050-3,250 (107: 3264/3208/3277; 24 extra depthwise convs fwd+bwd per step), final val loss 0.076-0.084 (107: 0.0822/0.0827/0.0836); RL sampling a few percent slower per token (12 small ops per cached step), totals 1,950-2,200 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks and CHANGED: Canon layers (causal depthwise conv over the last 4 residual states) before the attention and the MLP of every block
arch.norm: layernorm (Peri-LN blocks as in 107-claude: pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs); unchanged
arch.change: CHANGED vs 107-claude: model.blocks is six CanonBlock(256, 8) (subclass of 107's PeriLNBlock adding canon_a and canon_c depthwise Conv1d(256, 256, 4, groups=256, bias=False)). Block forward: x = canon_a(x); x = x + ln_attn_out(attn(ln1(x))); x = canon_c(x); x = x + ln_mlp_out(fc2(gelu(fc1(ln2(x))))), where canon(x)_t = x_t + conv over x_{t-3..t} with zero history at the sequence start. Width, heads, depth, RoPE, GELU, Peri-LN, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, optimizer and schedule unchanged. The canon layers persist into RL and eval
arch.n_params_detail: 107-claude's 4,800,000 + 12,288 canon taps = 4,812,288 (vocab 107). Checked on CPU with the pinned fork 51604b3 model.py
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from the fork, replace blocks with CanonBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state (keys blocks.i.canon_a.weight / canon_c.weight of shape (256, 1, 4) plus 107's ln_attn_out/ln_mlp_out). The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: fork attn/cache code unchanged; each canon layer keeps its previous 3 input rows in the block's cache dict under 'canon_a'/'canon_c' (B, 3, 256). Left pads in sample.generate_ids's prefill are zeroed (keep taken from the mask's last query row) so the first real token sees zero history exactly as in right-padded training. CPU check with the pinned fork: two left-padded prompts (8 and 17 tokens), cached prefill + 5 one-token steps vs full uncached forward per row, max abs logit diff 4.8e-7; prefill last-token logits vs unpadded forward 2.7e-7

canon.positions: Canon-A (residual stream before ln1/attention) and Canon-C (residual stream before ln2/MLP), one each per block, untied across blocks
canon.form: x_t <- x_t + sum_{i=0..3} w_i * x_{t-i} per channel (torch.nn.Conv1d(256, 256, 4, groups=256, bias=False) on a left-zero-padded sequence); no nonlinearity, no normalization
canon.init: PyTorch Conv1d default (kaiming uniform, fan_in 4): every weight ~ U(-0.5, 0.5), i.e. random, as in Allen-Zhu (2025)
canon.n_params: 6 blocks x 2 canon layers x 256 channels x 4 taps = 12,288
canon.optimizer: 3-D weights, so they fall into the AdamW auxiliary group (lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95) like the LayerNorms; Muon still sees exactly the same 25 matrices

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, ln_f) and CHANGED: + the 12 canon conv weights (256,1,4); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: As 107-claude (fork construction, blocks replaced and re-initialized with the fork _init, orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter, output LayerNorms gain 1 bias 0) plus CHANGED: canon conv weights at PyTorch's default U(-0.5, 0.5); nothing is zero-initialized, so at init each residual state is already a random 4-token causal mixture. RNG draws shift vs 107 because the convs consume generator state
